story: Tesla's new steering yoke isn't retro, it's a safety risk
text: >> Anyway, big rigs have loose steering because they need precision at highway speeds. The opposite is actually true. Big rigs have loose steering so that the driver will Not jack knife the truck in a panic situation. A tighter steering rack is Much more precise. Street tires, and especially racing tires, work best (have the most grip) at very narrow slip angles. Here's a Wikipedia about the "friction circle" as racers call it. " [LINK] " Here's a Great video shot at the Nürburgring showing an astonishing lap record of the Porsche 919 Hybrid race car, precision personified... Enjoy! " [VIDEO] "

> it will be pretty much destroyed next year by the Tesla S with plaid mode Why don't Tesla's current cars destroy the Taycan? I think it's fair to say that at this time Tesla's a year behind Porsche in the performance EV stakes. Here are some of the Taycan's performance test results which Tesla has so far been unable to match: - 24 hour endurance run. 3,425 kms covered in 24 hours: [LINK] - Onboard video of their 7:42 run at the Nurburgring: [LINK] - Acceleration and handling comparison to the Model S P100D: [LINK] - Model S Plaid's Nurburgring results: [LINK] And no onboard video yet from any of Tesla's Nurburgring runs unfortunately. It's also disappointing that Tesla isn't bringing any of its current cars to the Nurburgring. > the new roadster will literally lap it That seems unlikely. To literally lap the Taycan the new Roadster will need to achieve a 3:50 lap time. The current electric lap record is 6:05 held by the Volkswagen ID.R: [LINK] And the overall record is 5:19 held by the Porsche 919 Evo: [VIDEO]
